question_text: The dimensions of a block of land are measured to be $17\text{ m} \times 22\text{ m}$, rounded to the nearest metre. What are the boundary values for the actual area $A$ of the block of land?

subparts.stem: The dimensions of a block of land are measured to be $17\text{ m} \times 22\text{ m}$, rounded to the nearest metre. What are the boundary values for the actual area $A$ of the block of land?

mark_breakdown.desc: Finding upper and lower bounds for both dimensions
Multiplying corresponding lower and upper bounds

subparts.solution:
The width of the block could be from $16\frac{1}{2}\text{ m}$ to $17\frac{1}{2}\text{ m}$.
The length of the block could be from $21\frac{1}{2}\text{ m}$ to $22\frac{1}{2}\text{ m}$.
$\therefore$ the lower boundary of the area is $16\frac{1}{2} \times 21\frac{1}{2} = 354.75\text{ m}^2$
and the upper boundary of the area is $17\frac{1}{2} \times 22\frac{1}{2} = 393.75\text{ m}^2$.
$\therefore 354.75\text{ m}^2 < A < 393.75\text{ m}^2$

ai_explanation.concept_rule: Bounds of a product of positive measurements are found by multiplying the lower bounds for the minimum, and multiplying the upper bounds for the maximum.
step_by_step: Determine width bounds: $17 \pm 0.5$, which gives $16.5\text{ m}$ to $17.5\text{ m}$.
Determine length bounds: $22 \pm 0.5$, which gives $21.5\text{ m}$ to $22.5\text{ m}$.
Calculate lower boundary for area: $16.5 \times 21.5 = 354.75\text{ m}^2$.
Calculate upper boundary for area: $17.5 \times 22.5 = 393.75\text{ m}^2$.
State the inequality: $354.75\text{ m}^2 < A < 393.75\text{ m}^2$.
ai_explanation.common_pitfalls: Mixing a lower bound with an upper bound when looking for the extreme boundaries.
